$comment: Phase 1715 — the pinned prover for every model under proofs/ (BoundedFold.fst; check.ps1 carries the module list).
F* releases WEEKLY, and a proof is a claim about a specific prover: an unpinned toolchain
would silently change what the green tick means, and proof hints no longer exist to
stabilise it (--record_hints and --use_hints were removed from F*), so reproducibility
rests on this pin, on --quake, and on the margin in z3rlimit. The release bundles Z3, so
the pin covers the solver too, and z3version names which one is used.
The hash is over the downloaded archive; proofs/check.ps1 verifies it before extracting
and refuses to proceed on a mismatch.
The release, the hash and the flag sets are the ones the Fuaran-Core repository's proof
leg established and runs against. Matching it is deliberate: two repositories checking
against the same prover is what makes their claims comparable, and a different pin here
would need a reason of its own rather than an absence of one.

linux-x64.$comment: Declared but NOT hash-pinned: nothing in this repository has run the proof leg on Linux, and an unverified hash recorded as if it were verified is worse than an absent one. check.ps1 refuses a platform whose sha256 is empty and says why, and the push/PR job runs windows-latest for that reason. Phase 1848.D added the route out: the workflow_dispatch-only linux-pin job in .github/workflows/proofs.yml fetches this asset, PRINTS its SHA-256 and runs the leg on it through -FStarHome. Record the printed value here once that job is green - it then starts verifying the hash instead of printing it, with no further edit. If the leg cannot run on Linux at all, the posture is recorded as the proof-leg-windows-only policy claim in proofs.json rather than left undeclared.

flags.$comment: --report_assumes error is what makes an `assume` or an `admit` FAIL the leg rather than quietly weaken a theorem; it is not a strictness preference and must not be relaxed. --z3rlimit 60 against a module whose slowest query finishes well inside the default is a deliberate MARGIN, not a requirement: with hints gone, the thing that makes a check flaky is a query landing near the limit on a slower machine, and headroom is the cheapest defence available. `extract` carries no `--extract <module>`: check.ps1 appends one per module from its own list.
